A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same matching-market benchmark and LoRA experiments. All 37 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable; retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of LLMs on four preference-based tasks, prompting experiments, and LoRA fine-tuning results in Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical evaluations and adds tied-preference experiments in Figure 7 and fine-tuning sensitivity results in Table 8.

M1.justification: The synthetic reasoning-trace generation, LoRA training objective, main inference procedures, and Algorithms 1–5 remain unchanged. The additional backbone, prompting conditions, and hyperparameter variants extend evaluation without introducing a new proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates strict preference rankings. v2 Appendix E adds Easy IC and ML profiles containing ties, testing Gemini-2.5-Pro on weak, strong, and super stability. This is a targeted extension of the existing matching tasks; the original coverage remains.

E2.justification: Qwen3-32B is newly evaluated alongside DeepSeek-8B in the fine-tuning comparisons of Table 8. The original seven-model benchmark comparisons and existing prompting comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial evaluation designs: tied-profile outputs are classified under three stability criteria using baseline, STRONG, and SUPER prompts. Table 8 varies training culture, instance-size range, 5,000 versus 10,000 examples, LoRA rank 32 versus 64, and backbone. These are added experimental conditions; the original default settings remain stated as before.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's prompting and instability analyses, v2 adds systematic fine-tuning sensitivity tests addressing which training data and configurations support generalization. Appendix E also probes robustness to ties and explicit requests for stronger stability, including discussion of model reasoning traces.

E5.justification: Both versions specify Fisher's exact tests, Welch's t-tests, the p < 0.05 threshold, and fine-tuning seed 3407. v2 introduces no additional repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 7 and Table 8 add substantive findings about tied-preference failures and fine-tuning sensitivity. Table 2 also revises DeepSeek-8B's fine-tuned Easy/Medium success rates from 55%/44% to 64%/31%, and instability rates from 11.40/20.25 to 6.00/12.13, without explaining the revisions. Other original tables and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds definitions of weak, strong, and super stability, their implication hierarchy, possible nonexistence of stronger stable matchings, and cited algorithmic complexity statements. The original mathematical formulation and algorithms remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary retain the same central claims: a four-task benchmark, difficulty with large markets, compounding preference-reasoning errors, and LoRA improvements concentrated on smaller instances. The additional experiments do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that Gemini-2.5-Pro continues using deferred acceptance with ties, stronger-stability instructions may introduce noise, and easier or ML training instances are especially useful. Appendix J.1 newly explains structured inputs as separating reasoning failures from parsing. The conclusion acknowledges preliminary tied-preference coverage while retaining the broader limitations.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code and data release; v2 supplies a specific Data and Code repository link. It also documents Qwen3-32B's identifier, new ablation configurations, and tie-generation and prompt modifications. Existing hardware and default training details remain, and checkpoint release is still deferred.

R1.justification: v2 adds Irving's 'Stable marriage and indifference' and the National Resident Matching Program's 2024 report, supporting tied-preference algorithms and the interface-to-matching-systems motivation. The existing related-work discussion and principal research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introductory motivation and structured-input explanation, adds an appendix section, updates acknowledgments, and makes local grammatical and terminology corrections. The main narrative and section sequence are retained; later appendices are renumbered rather than replaced.

P2.justification: v2 adds a framework diagram as Figure 1, a tied-preference chart as Figure 7, and the sensitivity table as Table 8. Existing figures are retained with renumbering and relocation, and Table 3 now follows Table 2. The overall visual format remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The sensitivity experiments, preliminary tied-preference evaluation, clearer design rationale, and code/data access information modestly strengthen the paper. Reporting inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 8 gives default DeepSeek-8B ML success rates of 94% and 60%, while the retained Section 7 footnote claims 100% and above 80%. The central evidence and conclusions remain largely unchanged, so the additions support a limited overall improvement.
